To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the fatty acid composition of adipose tissue in rats is altered by hypothalamic lesions and that the changes are independent of the degree of obesity.

the composition of adipose tissue fat differs in obese rats from that of lean rats, the change in composition correlates with the degree of obesity attained, and that a change in fat composition can occur without weight gain.

(a) the fatty acid composition of adipose tissue is altered in obesity; (b) these changes are independent of the total body fat; (c) the change is a dynamic one and occurs within 48 hours after the onset of obesity; (d) the change is associated with increased rates of synthesis of fatty acids and triglycerides.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the metabolic events which accompany the development of obesity.
the study of metabolic changes which occur in the obese animal and their possible relevance to obesity in man.
the metabolic basis for the changes in the fatty acid composition of adipose tissue in obesity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the fatty acid composition of fat in the obese rat is not simply a function of the total amount, but is a reflection of the metabolic state of the animal, and is a sensitive index of the degree of obesity.
the changes in the fatty acid composition of adipose tissue are associated with the obesity of lesioned rats and are not a simple reflection of total body fat.
the fatty acid composition of adipose tissue is not fixed and is subject to dynamic changes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in obesity the fatty acid composition of adipose tissue is changed, the change being related to the amount of total body fat.

the changes in fatty acid composition of fat in obese rats are due to a change in the rate of synthesis of linoleic acid and that the rate of synthesis is increased in proportion to the degree of obesity.
the fatty acid composition of adipose tissue is not a fixed entity, but is subject to alteration by a variety of factors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the fatty acid profile of the fat in the liver, the fat around the organs, and the fat under the skin are different.
the fatty acids in the fat cells of people with obesity are different from those in people with healthy weight.
the fatty acids in our diet are not as important as the overall quality of the fats and oils we consume.
